requirements.evidence: Data model matches the task: migrations create_totems_table, create_totem_presets_table (login_code string(6) nullable unique) and create_totem_preset_queue_table (composite primary on preset_id/queue_id). Pairing command uses random_int + str_pad, a 10-minute expiry, clears consumed_at, writes an audit log and returns FAILURE for an unknown preset (TotemPairingCode.php:20-45). PairTotem.php:22-47 runs in a DB::transaction with lockForUpdate and returns one null for unknown/inactive/consumed/expired codes, so every case gets the same 401. Format check returns 400 (TotemAuthController.php:61-71). JWT carries all seven claims (TotemJwt.php:27-35). Middleware checks active flags, entity consistency and the queue intersection (TotemAuthenticate.php:44-60). Contracts are met: forbidden/queue_not_found/inactive_queue/invalid_priority; ticket issued via IssueTicket with TicketChannel::Totem and a 201 response; throttle:10,1 and throttle:30,1; a 429 rate_limited renderer; CORS for localhost/127.0.0.1 plus TOTEM_WEB_ORIGIN. .env.example, phpunit.xml and the docs are updated. No missing requirement found.

conventions.evidence: Pairing, a domain write, goes through a new App\Actions\PairTotem, and issuance reuses App\Actions\IssueTicket (TotemTicketController.php:40). Migrations have timestamped names and reversible down(). Models declare #[Fillable] and #[Hidden(['login_code'])]. CHANGELOG [Unreleased], docs/api/totem.md, database-schema.md, architecture.md, business-rules.md and ops/devops.md are updated. Deviations: queue-scope authorization is a hand-rolled check in an abstract base controller (TotemApiController.php:23-37) rather than a policy/gate. CORS is hand-rolled in a custom middleware even though the framework already provides it through config/cors.php, which this diff also adds.

security.evidence: HS256 decode rejects any alg other than HS256, compares signatures with hash_equals, uses strict base64url decoding and requires exp (TotemJwt.php:74-88). The missing-secret case fails closed with a RuntimeException. Queue lookup is scoped to the token's entity (`$this->entity($request)->queues()->where('slug', $slug)`), and scope is the intersection with the current pivot. Pairing has no oracle: one 401 for all failures, and the code is never logged (TotemAuthController.php:73-79). login_code is hidden from serialization. CORS has no credentials and sends no ACAO header for unknown origins. Priority is validated strictly as an int from the allowed list before any write. Only a nit: the 32-character minimum secret length is documented but not enforced at runtime.

tests.evidence: Pest feature tests cover: pairing command (code format, expiry, replacement, unknown preset), auth success with claim checks, 400 for six malformed inputs, a single 401 for expired/consumed/inactive/unknown codes, single-use consumption, the 10/min throttle, codes kept out of logs (TotemPairingTest.php). They also cover missing, malformed, tampered and expired tokens, inactive totem and preset, entity mismatch, last_seen_at, scope intersection, cross-entity 404, inactive_queue, invalid_priority with six datasets, sequential A001/A002 with channel totem, and the 30/min throttle (TotemApiTest.php). CORS tests include preflight, unknown origin, configured origin and a 429 response that keeps CORS headers. Missing: no test for a deleted totem/preset row or for an alg=none/other-alg token, and `expect($token)->toBeString()` in the mismatch test asserts nothing useful.

simplicity.evidence: CORS is implemented twice. config/cors.php (new, used by Laravel's built-in HandleCors) defines the same localhost/127.0.0.1 patterns, methods and headers as the custom TotemCors middleware (TotemCors.php:11, 85-93). The custom middleware is prepended globally and also hooked into $exceptions->respond in bootstrap/app.php. One mechanism, the native one, would do. The rest is lean: a small HS256 class (permitted by the task), TicketPriority as the single source of priority values, and a thin shared base controller.

readability.evidence: Classes are small and well named, and the PHPDoc explains intent, for example the oracle comment in PairTotem.php:11-18 and the trimStrings comment in bootstrap/app.php. Minor issues: controllers take `string $entitySlug` but never use it and instead read `$request->route('entity')` in entityMismatch(). Request attributes ('totem_entity', 'totem_queue_ids') are untyped string keys shared between the middleware and the controllers. TotemAuthenticate's last condition `$preset->entity_id !== $totem->entity_id` is redundant after the two checks before it.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task. Small extras: the global trimStrings exception for api/* (bootstrap/app.php) changes framework behaviour for the whole API to serve the pairing-code format check. The redundant config/cors.php duplicates the custom middleware. The devops.md secrets table update is related and appropriate.

issues.explanation: CORS rules are defined twice: the new config/cors.php drives Laravel's built-in HandleCors, and a custom global middleware plus an exception-response hook reimplement the same origin patterns, so two sources of truth can drift apart.
Queue-scope authorization (403 forbidden) is an ad-hoc controller check rather than going through a policy/gate as the conventions require for authorization.
No test covers a deleted totem/preset row or a token signed with a different alg, and the entity-mismatch test ends with a meaningless `expect($token)->toBeString()`.
The `$entitySlug` route parameter is accepted but unused, while the base class re-reads `$request->route('entity')`.
String trimming is disabled for the whole API to support one format check; this is defensible but is a broader global change than the task needed.
The documented 32+ character minimum secret length is not enforced; any non-empty secret is accepted.

review.summary: The change implements the totem BFF fully: schema, models and factories, an atomic PairTotem action, the pairing command, a correct small HS256 JWT, an auth middleware with live queue-scope intersection, the four endpoints reusing IssueTicket, throttling with JSON 429s, localhost CORS and updated docs. It is backed by thorough Pest tests. The main drawback is CORS defined twice (custom global middleware plus config/cors.php), along with minor convention and test-coverage gaps, so I would approve it with small follow-ups.
